title: Hearing Dallas bands; Texas players he met only afterwards
summary: He slipped into Dallas dance halls but never the hotels, and met nearly all the Texas musicians (Tyree Glenn, Budd Johnson and others) only later.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, I used to go and listen to a lot of bands in Dallas.
Can you remember what different -- like, at the hotels, or did you ever get into those --
No, I never got into a hotel there in Dallas, at all.
The reason that T-Bone did, you see, was because he used to -- they'd let him in and he'd get out on the floor, you see, and throw money.
Yeah, that's right.
That's it, and that way he'd hear some of those bands that came through.
Sure.
So that way, he'd hear it. So actually none of the musicians that you know today that you actually knew then.
Not personally.
Well, what about Tyree Glenn?
When I met Tyree Glenn was in New York, and I worked with him.
Gee, that's funny, Gus. What a funny thing, huh?
Yeah, that's right.
So, really, no, none of them.
I didn't know them personally at all, not at all.
No. That's a funny thing, isn't it?
I only met them afterwards.
Yeah, right.
We'd sit down and start talking.
And you'd discover that --
And then we'd discover about things. It's like Budd Johnson, see.
Well, that's right. I was going to -- and Keg. And Keg.

He's Dallas.
He's Dallas.
Yes, yes.

No, I didn't know him then, see.
Yeah.

Oh, that's it, then. He is older than you are. all right. Yes, that's right.

Yeah. You didn't know a boy called Clarence Seymour, did you? He wasn't a musician, but he was -- he lived -- Clarence Seymour.

Yeah, I just wondered, because he --
Seymour.
Seymour, yeah.
He's from Dallas?

North Dallas.
